stages.title: Advanced vocabulary and terminology
stages.hook: Why do doctors say "hipertensión" and not "presión muy alta"? Where do technical words in Spanish come from?
explain: Advanced Spanish vocabulary draws mainly on Latin, with Greek roots in science and medicine (hipo-, hiper-, -logía), Arabic words from the Middle Ages (aceite, azúcar, ojalá), and later borrowings from indigenous languages, French and English. Knowing roots helps: bio (vida), geo (tierra), grafía (escritura), crono (tiempo).

Connotation matters: "económico" is neutral or positive, "barato" can sound cheap. Register distinguishes "automóvil" (formal), "coche" (everyday). Nominalisation turns verbs into nouns for a formal style: "decidir" becomes "la decisión". Cognates between Spanish and English aid reading, but check false friends.
stages.mnemonic: Latín en la raíz, árabe en el azúcar, náhuatl en el chocolate.

gq.q: Which word in Spanish comes from Arabic?
What does the root "crono" refer to?
gq.why: Crono comes from Greek khronos, time.

panel.q: Why does Spanish have many words from Arabic?
o: Arabic-speaking peoples ruled much of the Iberian Peninsula for centuries
panel.why: Contact from 711 until the fifteenth century left lasting traces, especially in words beginning with al-.

panel.q: What is the purpose of nominalisation in formal writing?
panel.model: Turning verbs into nouns (decidir to la decisión) makes the style more formal, compact and abstract.
panel.why: Nominal style.

panel.q: Which pair has similar meaning but different tone?
panel.why: Automóvil is more formal than coche.

teach.topic: Where advanced Spanish words come from
teach.model: Many Spanish words come from Latin. Science uses Greek roots. Arabic gave words like azúcar. Learn roots and suffixes to guess meaning, and notice tone and register.

points.ask: How can I guess a word?
Do similar words feel the same?

stages.title: Academic language
stages.hook: Why do academic papers in Spanish say "se observa que" and not "yo veo que"?
explain: Academic Spanish is impersonal and precise. It uses the pasiva refleja ("se analizaron los datos"), the first person plural "nosotros" of modesty ("hemos observado"), nominal phrases and cautious verbs: "parece indicar", "sugiere que". Use connectors like "por consiguiente", "en cambio", "cabe destacar que".

Cite sources consistently: "según García (2020)", or footnotes. Plagiarism means presenting others' ideas as your own. Paraphrase and credit the source. Structure follows introducción, marco teórico, metodología, resultados, discusión y conclusiones. Avoid colloquialisms and unsupported generalisations.
stages.mnemonic: Se + verb: the passive that hides the actor.
sentences: It is worth noting this result.
According to García, the cause is social.

gq.q: Which sentence is most suitable for academic style?
o: Se observa una relación entre ambos factores.
Yo creo que esto es genial y muy interesante, ¿no?
gq.why: The impersonal se is a typical formal strategy.

o: a question that the writer asks the reader
gq.why: It means "it should be noted that".

panel.q: "Se analizaron los datos" agrees with datos because...
o: datos is the plural subject of the reflexive passive
panel.why: In the pasiva refleja the verb agrees with the grammatical subject.

panel.q: Why is hedging ("parece indicar") used in research writing?
panel.model: It keeps claims proportionate to the evidence and avoids stating more than the data prove.
panel.why: Epistemic modality.

panel.q: What is plagiarism?
o: Using someone else's work without credit
Writing too fast without checking spelling
panel.why: Honest scholarship requires acknowledging sources.

teach.model: Academic Spanish is formal and impersonal. It uses se plus a verb to avoid naming the doer. Use connectors like por consiguiente. Support claims with sources and use cautious verbs.

points.ask: How do I avoid saying I?

stages.title: Professional communication
stages.hook: An email ends "Quedo a la espera de sus noticias." Why not just "Contesten rápido"?
explain: Professional Spanish values courtesy and clarity. Emails open with "Estimada señora Pérez:" and state the reason: "Le escribo para confirmar...". The conditional and the subjunctive soften requests: "Le agradecería que me enviara...". Close with "Atentamente" or "Cordialmente".

At work, titles matter: "Licenciado", "ingeniero", "doctora" are used in Latin America as respectful forms. Meeting phrases: "Pasemos al siguiente punto", "Propongo que...", "Quedamos en...". Cultural expectations about time, hierarchy and small talk vary across Spanish-speaking countries, so observe and adapt.
items: I would appreciate it if you sent
let us move to the next item
sentences: I am writing to confirm the meeting.
Let us move on to the next item.

gq.why: The conditional and imperfect subjunctive soften the request.

gq.q: What does "adjunto" mean in an email?

panel.q: Why do formal emails use "usted" and its forms?
o: It shows respect and professional distance
panel.why: Usted marks formality.

panel.q: Why might a workplace in Mexico and one in Spain differ in how direct requests are?
panel.model: Cultural norms about hierarchy and politeness differ, so the same request may be phrased more or less directly.
panel.why: Intercultural pragmatics.

panel.q: Which closing suits a formal business email?
panel.why: Cordialmente is a standard business closing.

teach.model: At work, be polite and clear. Start with the reason for writing. Use usted and soften requests with the conditional. End with a closing like Atentamente. Cultures differ, so observe how people speak.

points.ask: How do I make it polite?

stages.title: Literary analysis
stages.hook: "Verde que te quiero verde." Why does a line of poetry by Lorca still move readers?
explain: Literary analysis asks how language creates meaning: imagery, metaphor, symbol, rhythm, narrative voice and structure. In Spanish poetry, metre is counted in syllables. The most common line has eight syllables (octosílabo), and the eleven-syllable line (endecasílabo) is used in sonnets. Rhyme can be consonante (all sounds repeat) or asonante (only vowels).

Federico García Lorca (Spain) used rich imagery in the "Romancero gitano". Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz (Mexico), Miguel de Cervantes ("Don Quijote"), Gabriela Mistral (Chile) and Julio Cortázar (Argentina) are major voices. A close reading quotes short passages and explains their effect, linking form to theme.
stages.mnemonic: Cita, nombra el recurso, explica el efecto.

gq.q: How many syllables does an endecasílabo have?

gq.why: In asonante rhyme, only the vowels from the last stressed vowel onward match.

panel.q: Which statement is a supported interpretation?
o: The repeated green suggests desire and danger, in stanza one.
The poet was probably sad when writing it, because poems are sad
panel.why: Good analysis links a claim to textual detail.

panel.q: Why is the narrator not always the author?
panel.model: The narrator is a voice invented by the author and may have limits or biases that the author does not share.
panel.why: Narrative voice.

panel.q: Who wrote "Don Quijote"?
panel.why: Cervantes published Don Quijote in 1605 and 1615.

teach.model: Look at the images, symbols, voice and sound of a text. In poetry, count syllables and check rhyme. Quote short passages and explain what effect they have. Do not confuse narrator and author.

points.ask: How do I support my reading?

stages.title: Advanced listening comprehension
stages.hook: Why does a speaker from the Caribbean seem to swallow the final s, while a speaker from Madrid pronounces it clearly? Can you follow both?
explain: Advanced listening means following authentic speech at natural speed with different accents. Caribbean and coastal varieties often weaken final s and r; Andean varieties keep s clear; Rioplatense speakers use sh-like sounds for y and ll ("sheísmo"); Castilian Spanish distinguishes z/c from s. Fast speech brings contractions in rhythm and word linking.

Strategies: predict from context, use stress and intonation, notice discourse markers ("o sea", "pues"), and tolerate unknown words. In lectures, listen for signposts ("en segundo lugar") and for emphasis. Take notes on key words, then reconstruct meaning. Podcasts, radio and films from several countries build range.
stages.mnemonic: No oigas solo las palabras: escucha el sentido.
sentences: I take notes during the lecture.

o: A sh-like sound for y and ll in Rioplatense Spanish
Dropping all the vowels in fast speech
A kind of grammar used only in the River Plate region
gq.why: It is typical of Buenos Aires and Montevideo.

gq.q: What helps most when you meet an unfamiliar accent?
o: Stopping at the first unknown word
gq.why: Extensive listening and context help adaptation.

panel.q: Why can final s weakening make verbs ambiguous?
o: Tú hablas can sound like tú habla
Hablas becomes a noun in fast speech
panel.why: Listeners use context and pronouns to recover the person.

panel.q: How can you listen effectively to a lecture in Spanish?
panel.model: Listen for signposts and the main idea, take notes on key words and use context to fill gaps.
panel.why: Listening strategies.

panel.q: Which feature is typical of fast, informal speech?
o: Words blend together and some sounds weaken
Every sound is stressed equally and clearly heard
panel.why: Connected speech reduces and links sounds.

teach.model: Spanish sounds different in different places. Some speakers weaken the final s. Use context, stress and key words to follow. Listen to speakers from many countries to get used to them.

stages.title: Oral fluency and presentations
stages.hook: How can you speak for two minutes in Spanish without notes?
explain: Fluency means smooth flow rather than perfection. Use chunks (bloques) such as "en mi opinión", "a mi modo de ver", "lo que quiero decir es que". Use fillers like "bueno", "pues", "este" (Mexico) or "eh" to think. Organise a talk in three parts: introduction, development, conclusion.

Vary your pitch and speed, pause before key ideas, and stress key words. Practise rhythm: Spanish is syllable-timed, so syllables have similar length. Use the subjunctive and connectors to sound natural: "Aunque sea difícil...", "Es posible que...". Record yourself to notice pace and repeated errors.
items: lo que quiero decir es que
sentences: In my opinion, it is necessary.
It is possible that it rains.

gq.why: Syllables tend to have similar duration.
En mi opinión means in my opinion.

panel.q: What is a benefit of recording yourself?
o: You notice pace, errors and fillers
panel.why: Self-monitoring improves speaking.

panel.q: Why are chunks useful for fluency?
panel.model: They are ready-made phrases that can be retrieved quickly, so speech flows more naturally.
panel.why: Formulaic language.

panel.q: Which sentence correctly uses the subjunctive after an expression of possibility?
panel.why: Es posible que is followed by the subjunctive.

teach.model: Use ready-made phrases to keep flowing. Plan three parts: opening, main ideas, ending. Pause before key points. Record yourself and listen for ways to improve.

stages.title: Translation and interpretation
stages.hook: "Estoy de acuerdo" is "I agree", not "I am of agreement". How do translators decide?
explain: Translators work with source and target languages. Procedures include literal translation, calque, transposition (changing word class), modulation (changing point of view) and adaptation. For example "Se prohíbe fumar" becomes "No smoking" or "Smoking is prohibited". The right choice depends on text type, readers and purpose.

Interpreters work consecutively (the speaker pauses) or simultaneously (almost in real time). They need memory, note-taking and quick decisions. Ethics: faithfulness, impartiality and confidentiality. When a term has no equivalent, translators may keep the original with a gloss. Be careful with false friends such as "realizar", "asistir" and "sensible".
stages.mnemonic: Fiel al sentido, natural en la lengua de llegada.
sentences: We keep the term with a note.

gq.q: Which interpreting mode works almost in real time?
gq.why: Simultaneous interpreters speak while the speaker continues.

gq.q: "Se prohíbe fumar" is naturally rendered as...
gq.why: Notices such as signs use conventional short forms, so Se prohíbe fumar becomes No smoking.

panel.q: What is modulation in translation?
o: Changing the point of view while keeping the meaning
Changing the font and layout of the whole translated text
panel.why: For example, "no tardes" can become "be quick".

panel.q: Why must an interpreter be impartial and keep information confidential?
panel.model: Parties need to trust that the interpreter conveys messages accurately and keeps private information safe.
panel.why: Professional ethics.

panel.q: A text says "El Gobierno estudiará el asunto". The English "will look into the matter" is...
panel.why: It conveys the meaning with a natural English phrase.

teach.model: A translator works with written text, an interpreter with speech. Both keep the meaning and make it sound natural in the new language. They must be accurate and keep information private.

stages.title: Idiomatic and figurative language
stages.hook: "Hacer una montaña de un grano de arena" - is the speaker really building a mountain?
explain: Figurative language includes metaphor ("el tiempo es oro"), simile, hyperbole ("te lo dije mil veces"), personification, metonymy ("leer a Cervantes") and irony. Spanish has many idioms and refranes: "No hay mal que por bien no venga", "Camarón que se duerme se lo lleva la corriente", "Quien mucho abarca poco aprieta".

Many idioms depend on culture: "estar en el quinto pino" (to be very far away), "tomar el pelo" (to pull someone's leg), "echar una mano" (to lend a hand), "ser uña y carne" (to be inseparable). Idioms vary by country, such as "chévere" in Colombia and Venezuela and "guay" in Spain. Translate the meaning, not the image.
stages.mnemonic: La imagen engaña; el sentido manda.
items: hacer una montaña de un grano de arena
every cloud has a silver lining
no hay mal que por bien no venga

gq.why: It is an idiom for joking at someone's expense.

gq.q: "Te lo he dicho mil veces" is an example of...
gq.why: The number is exaggerated for emphasis.

panel.q: Why should you not translate idioms literally?
o: The meaning is figurative and not the sum of the words
panel.why: Idioms are fixed units with conventional meaning.

panel.q: Why do idioms vary between Spanish-speaking countries?
panel.model: Each region has its own history and culture, so expressions and slang develop differently and are not always shared.
panel.why: Dialect variation.

panel.q: "Leer a Cervantes" uses metonymy because...
o: the author stands for his works
Cervantes is a verb in this sentence
panel.why: The writer's name replaces the books.

teach.model: Figurative language means more than the literal words. A metaphor says one thing is another and hyperbole exaggerates. An idiom is a fixed phrase with a special meaning. Do not translate it word by word.

points.ask: How do I understand or translate it?

stages.title: Extended independent writing
stages.hook: How do you plan and write 800 words in Spanish on your own?
explain: Independent writing is a process: plan (lluvia de ideas, esquema), draft (borrador), revise (revisar) and edit (corregir). Choose a purpose (informar, argumentar, narrar, describir) and a reader. Begin with a thesis or an interesting opening, develop each paragraph around one idea, and close with a conclusion.

Check cohesion with connectors and pronouns, and check coherence by reading the sentence order. Control verb tenses (do not mix preterite and imperfect by accident), agreement of gender and number, accents, and punctuation including ¿?, ¡!, and the comma rules. Vary sentence length. Show, do not tell: "le temblaban las manos" instead of "estaba nerviosa".

gq.q: Which step comes after the draft?
gq.why: Revise content and organisation after drafting.

gq.q: Which sentence shows rather than tells?
gq.why: Concrete detail lets the reader infer emotion.

panel.q: Why is it incorrect to write "a ver" for "haber" in "Debe haber una razón"?
o: They are different words with different meanings
They are the same word with two different spellings
panel.why: A ver means let's see; haber is the verb to have/there to be.

panel.q: What should you check when you edit a Spanish text?
panel.model: Check accents and spelling, agreement of gender and number, verb tenses and punctuation.
panel.why: Editing checklist.

panel.q: What is the difference between revising and editing?
o: Revising improves ideas and order; editing corrects small errors
Editing comes before drafting and revising comes at the very end
panel.why: Revise first for big issues, then edit for details.

teach.topic: Writing a long text in Spanish
teach.model: Plan first, then write a draft, then revise the ideas and edit the details. Keep one idea in each paragraph. Check tenses, agreement and accents. Use connectors to link ideas.
